capex.item: Company plans to spend approximately INR 1,200 crores of capex over the three years FY26, FY27 and FY28, starting April 2025.
capex.quote: the company plans to incur approx. 1200 crores capex over the period of next three years

capex.item: The company has begun executing an INR1,200 crore capex plan spanning FY26 to FY28 at Silvassa and Waghodia to raise cable capacity.
capex.quote: We have already begun executing our INR1,200 crores capex plan in FY '26 to FY '28, primarily aimed to increase cable capacity to support a 15% to 20% volume growth

capex.item: Company is executing a capex plan of about Rs 1,200 crores over a period of 3 years, with almost 80% to be invested on the cable side, sized to service 18% annual volume growth.
capex.quote: our capex plan where we have planned to invest around INR1,200 crores over a period of 3 years, in which like almost 80% will be invested in cable side only

capex.item: Rs 1,200 crore capex program for FY26-FY28 to expand cable and wire capacity is progressing as planned, with about Rs 300 crore already spent in FY26 and the majority of the outflow due in FY27.
capex.quote: What we have planned, like investment of INR1,200 crore, out of which, almost INR300 crores we have invested in FY26 already.

capex.item: RR Kabel committed total capex of INR 1,200 Crores under Project RRise (FY26-FY28), targeting a 1.7x capacity multiple over three years.
capex.quote: INR 1,200 Crores Total Capex Committed / 1.7x Capacity Multiple over Three Years

capex.item: The first tranche of the INR 1,200 Crore three-year capex programme was deployed in FY26 as modular expansions at the Silvassa and Waghodia facilities, integrated biannually to align with demand.
capex.quote: This drove the execution of the initial phase of our INR 1,200 Crore three-year capital expenditure programme, with the first tranche deployed in FY 2025-26. These augmentations at the Silvassa and Waghodia facilities are being implemented as modular expansions integrated biannually

capex.item: The existing INR 500 crores capex plan spread over the last two years is on track, with the majority completed by March 2025 and a few capacities added by September 2025.
capex.quote: the majority of the capex will get completed by March '25 and a few like capacity will be added out of this capex by September '25 also

capex.item: The earlier INR500 crore capex is on the verge of completion during FY26 and will deliver full capacity this year.
capex.quote: apart from INR500 crores capex, what we have already announced, and it is on verge of completion in this year. Majority part was already executed.

capex.item: The Rs 1,200 crore capex will lift cable manufacturing capability from 66 KV today to 220 KV, with part coming in mid-FY27 and completion by FY28.
capex.quote: With new capex plan, we'll be able to achieve capability to build up to 220 KV... it will get completed by FY2028.

capex.item: The INR 1,200 crores capex will be a brownfield project at the existing Waghodia facility near Vadodara, with almost 80% directed to cables.
capex.quote: this will be like brownfield project in the existing facility at Waghodia, which is near Vadodara... Almost 80% will go in the cable

capex.item: Cable capacity will be added in tranches every six months rather than in one block, to match the 18% volume growth plan given cable utilisation is already above 90%.
capex.quote: In every six months we'll keep adding few capacities.

capex.item: The new expansion adds 36,000 tons of cable capacity at Waghodia plus 18,000 tons of wire capacity at Silvassa, taking blended company capacity to 1.7x current levels.
capex.quote: we are investing in manufacturing with a 1.7x increase in capacity at Silvassa and Waghodia... it is not only 36,000 tons, but it is a combination of 36,000 plus 18,000 tons

capex.item: FMEG capex will remain small at roughly INR 20-25 crores as about two-thirds of FMEG revenue is sourced from third parties on a trading basis.
capex.quote: in FMEG, we have not made any big capex plan. It will be very small, like in the range of INR 20 crores, INR 25 crores only

capex.item: Capacity from the first year of the new INR1,200 crore expansion will only start contributing from mid-FY27 onwards.
capex.quote: out of this in first year, whatever we invest we'll get -- give me capacity maybe after mid of FY '27 onwards only

bull_bear.body: Dividend INR 9.50/share for FY26 (INR 5.50 final); Reinvestment in capacity expansion (Project RRise); Working capital optimization via LC facilities.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension in Middle East (12% of total top line, 40% of exports) causing shipment delays; Copper price volatility impacting working capital and pass-through timing; FMEG breakeven delay; Potential industry capacity addition (though mgmt sees no oversupply risk for their mix).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth (16-18% CAGR); Pragmatic on near-term geopolitical noise; Disciplined on pricing and cost control; Transparent on FMEG delays.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Inventory bloat is largely 'Stock-in-Transit' (SIT) due to war-related shipping delays rather than demand slowdown; Data center opportunity is immediate using existing product suite (no new R&D wait time) but requires approval cycles; Cable mix shift (27% to ~31%) driven more by volume/capacity than just price, enabling better operating leverage.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The balance sheet has been progressively de-levered, with debt-to-equity falling from 0.4x (FY23) to 0.1x in FY25 and FY26 and non-current borrowings effectively nil at INR 10 Mn.
- Growth has been funded internally, with cumulative FY23-FY26 operating cash flow comfortably covering investing outflows and financing consistently a net outflow (INR 1,620 Mn in FY26).
- Other equity has compounded from INR 9,567 Mn (FY23) to INR 25,178 Mn (FY26) with share capital essentially flat, indicating retained-earnings-led capital building rather than equity issuance.
- Return ratios have improved materially over FY23-FY26, reaching 20.8% and 25.8% in FY26 versus 14.2% and 15.3% in FY23.
- The deck makes no mention of dividend policy, buybacks or a stated payout framework.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- One of the broadest international certification portfolios among Indian Wires & Cables manufacturers (42 approvals) providing market-access credentials across 66+ countries
- Fully integrated manufacturing model producing its own insulation and sheathing compounds in-house (backward-integrated aluminium rods and compound production), controlling quality at the formulation level rather than just the production line
- Loyalty ecosystem of 6,65,000+ electricians and 2,15,000+ retailers that converts the distribution network into a brand-advocacy network
- Broad distribution reach of 7,200+ distributors and dealers across India
- Management team with deep industry roots and a forward-looking mindset
- RR Signature premium sub-brand strategy (60-65% of fan revenue in FY26) capturing the trading-up consumer
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility (copper, aluminium, PVC/polymers) — Copper fluctuated significantly in Q4FY26 and LME copper/aluminium benchmarks remain volatile; management mitigates via long-term procurement contracts, diversified suppliers, dynamic price pass-through in B2C and 100% back-to-back procurement for B2B export orders, but margins remain exposed to sharp swings.
- Geopolitical and maritime supply-chain disruption — Ongoing Middle East conflict and Red Sea maritime disruptions escalated ocean freight rates, extended transit times and inflated war-risk insurance premiums, and caused an expansion in Sales-in-Transit inventories during the year.
- Export / geographic concentration in the Middle East — The Middle East contributes approximately 40% of total export revenues (roughly 12% of consolidated revenue), making the Company disproportionately exposed to regional conflict, trade-policy shifts and shipping-route disruption in that geography.
- Intense price competition — Management explicitly flags intense price competition from both large organised peers and unorganised local players as a threat to margins and market share.
- Global trade-policy and tariff uncertainty — Potential changes in global trade policies and tariff structures in key export markets (alongside evolving US tariff policy) create pricing and demand uncertainty for the export business.
- FMEG segment remains loss-making amid a constrained discretionary demand environment — Despite narrowing losses (down 28% YoY) and a stated FY27 break-even roadmap, the FMEG segment reported an operating loss in FY26 and operates in a discretionary-spend category exposed to weak consumer sentiment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Wires & Cables: 90% of FY26 revenue (INR 8,764cr, +31% YoY), Segment Profit INR 776cr (+56% YoY); FMEG: 10% of revenue (INR 959cr, +3% YoY), losses narrowing, breakeven delayed to FY27 (from FY26) due to weather/input cost lag.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The business is run as two reported segments: Wires & Cables at 91% of Q1 FY27 revenue and FMEG at 9%, with W&C the profit engine and FMEG the scale-building bet.
- Exports are a structural, not incidental, part of the mix at roughly 25-29% of revenue across the last four reported quarters, giving a demand base beyond India.
- Management frames W&C growth as outperformance versus the industry, attributing it to volume growth, execution and favourable industry dynamics rather than pricing alone.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: RR Kabel is a wires-and-cables and FMEG manufacturer serving residential, commercial, industrial and infrastructure customers in India and 66+ export countries. The Wires & Cables portfolio (house wires, industrial wires, power cables, specialty cables, solar cables) is the primary business (~90% of revenue), while the FMEG portfolio (fans, lighting, switches, switchgear, appliances and kitchen appliances) is a smaller, distribution-led consumer business (~10% of revenue).
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Wires & Cables:** House Wires (FR, HR+FR, FRLS, LS0H-EBXL), Industrial Wires, Control & Instrumentation Cables, Fire Survival Cables (IS 17505-1 & LPCB Approved), Data & Communication Cables, LV/MV Power Cables (up to 33 kV), HV Power Cables (up to 66 kV), Solar DC Cables, Specialty Cables
- **FMEG:** Fans (RR Signature & Luminous), Lighting & Luminaires, Switches & Switchgears (modular switch plates, sockets, regulators, MCBs, RCCBs, Distribution Boards), Home & Kitchen Appliances (induction/infra-red cooktops, mixer grinders, hand blenders, water heaters, room heaters, irons, air coolers)

latest_quarter.body: Raw material (Copper, Al, PVC) volatility managed via continuous pricing pass-through (2-3% triggers); FY26 margin expansion of 130bps achieved; FY27 guidance 9.5% despite elevated copper base; FMEG margins pressured by input cost lag.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~30% FY27 (implied mathematically by 16-18% volume + price rise); Margin: Targeting 9.5% EBIT for W&C in FY27, 10.5% by FY28 (300bps expansion roadmap); Order Inflow: Strong B2B/Infra focus; Capex: INR 1,200cr program (FY26-FY28), INR 300cr spent in FY26, majority spend in FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Management cites >90% capacity utilization in cables; no specific value given, but demand described as 'healthy' domestically and 'stronger' in exports excluding Middle East disruption; B2B segment scaling rapidly.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: HV/EHV Cable expansion (66KV to 220KV capability) targeting infra/wind/solar/data centers; B2B channel deepening; Export diversification beyond Middle East; FMEG turnaround to breakeven in FY27 with 20-25% value growth target.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Project RRise: a three-year (FY26-FY28) roadmap shifting from broad market expansion to targeted, margin-accretive execution, building healthy sustainable margins through cost optimisation, improved product mix and greater operating efficiency
- Re-engineer the W&C product mix to favour the B2B institutional cable market over the retail-heavy wire segment, seeking longer-term contract visibility, stickier institutional relationships and a more predictable cash-flow profile
- Deploy capex in modular, biannual tranches at the Silvassa and Waghodia facilities calibrated precisely to demand, protecting ROCE by avoiding capital deployment ahead of demand / idle capacity
- In FMEG, prioritise high-margin premiumisation over top-line volume; expand the RR Signature premium sub-brand (kitchen essentials - mixer grinders, electric cooktops, hand blenders - launched April 2026)
- Deepen B2B partnerships with industrial and corporate customers through wider reach, stronger engagement and consistently reliable, high-quality products
- Strengthen export presence in the Middle East and Europe, positioning to benefit from a prospective EU-India trade agreement
- Optimise cost structure through renewable energy adoption and automation
- Leadership structure realigned to a Joint Managing Director model: Mahhesh Kabra to lead new product development and operational excellence; Rajesh Kabra to lead strategic business development and market expansion (domestic and international)
- The Company follows a Dividend Distribution Policy under which the Board declares an interim dividend during the year and recommends a final dividend at year-end, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, reflecting a stated commitment to creating and sharing value with shareholders alongside continued reinvestment into growth (including the Project RRise capex programme).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Under the three-year 'Project RRise' roadmap (FY26-FY28), RR Kabel committed a three-year capital expenditure programme with the first tranche deployed in FY26 as modular expansions at the Silvassa and Waghodia facilities, integrated biannually to align precisely with demand and protect ROCE. Strategic capex was specifically deployed at Waghodia to support the B2B/cable volume scale-up. Separately, capital investments during FY26 upgraded manufacturing infrastructure to add capacity for e-beam cross-linked solar cables (EN 50618 and IEC 62930 certified, UV-resistant, halogen-free) and expanded capacity for fire-resistant, low-smoke cable variants (BS 6724, UL 44, LPCB-certified). On the captive-power side, the Company expanded its hybrid solar-wind renewable energy project during the year, adding 9.6 MW of capacity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Data centre build-out is a major demand catalyst, requiring markedly higher cable-density per square foot than traditional industrial projects due to redundancy and zero-downtime requirements
- Transition to green energy infrastructure (solar, wind, transmission grid expansion, rural electrification) is creating multi-year demand cycles for specialised cabling
- Domestic economy provided a supportive operating environment (infrastructure capex, affordable housing, EV adoption, rising incomes) even as the global environment was volatile with Middle East shipping disruptions and copper/aluminium/PVC price volatility
- Year-end inventory was elevated due to Sales-in-Transit (SIT) caused by Middle East shipping disruptions; management expects this timing difference to normalise in coming quarters
- Cable volumes are structurally outpacing wire volumes, reflecting a B2B/institutional demand shift; cable lines ran at high utilisation through the year
- Housing wire demand is structurally tied to residential completions, with premiumisation (FR-LSH, energy-efficient variants) and smart-home wiring content (~30% more wiring per home) as additional demand accelerants
- Wire and cable market is formalising, with the organised segment's share rising (regulatory tailwinds: BIS certification mandates, National Building Code fire-safety enforcement, state electricity board compliance audits) at the expense of the unorganised segment
- Specialty and industrial cables are the fastest-growing sub-segment, driven by data centres, pharmaceutical manufacturing, industrial automation and solar/high-voltage grid-tie demand
- Export demand faced Middle East geopolitical headwinds but showed resilience, with the Middle East remaining the core geography for international operations

deepdive.thesis: RR Kabel delivered record Q4/FY26 revenue and PAT driven by 31% W&C volume growth and pricing, though Middle East geopolitical tensions created a transient export headwind in March/April; the strategic pivot to HV cables (up to 220KV) via INR 1,200cr capex positions it for higher margins and data center/infra orders despite near-term inventory build-up from goods-in-transit.

open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of INR 5.50 per equity share for FY26 (cash outflow of approximately INR 6,221 Lakhs), subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM; record date 16 June 2026.
Company is targeting around 8.5% EBITDA margin on a yearly basis and expects FY26 to land in that line rather than guiding a specific Q4 number.
FMEG segment is planned to turn green at EBIT level (breakeven) in Q4 FY26, with Q3 losses already narrowed to about Rs 5 crores.
Company has planned for 18% volume growth on a yearly basis in wires & cables and says capacity is being added in phased manner to service it.
Management expects to improve EBITDA margins by about 100 basis points in the coming year, driven by scale, efficiency and better product mix.

open.horizon: FY26 and each of next 3 years
open.item: Management guides to 18% year-on-year volume growth in the Wires & Cables segment, majorly driven by cables.
Management committed to achieving breakeven in the FMEG segment in FY26 (indicated as possibly in H1FY26).
The earlier INR500 crore capex is on the verge of completion during FY26 and will deliver full capacity this year.
Cable revenue contribution is targeted to rise from 30% to 35% of the mix, shifting the wire:cable ratio to 65:35 by next year end, in both domestic and export.
FMEG capex will remain small at roughly INR 20-25 crores as about two-thirds of FMEG revenue is sourced from third parties on a trading basis.
Management flagged that the Middle East war will hit Q1FY27 exports harder than Q4FY26, with the Middle East accounting for about 12% of overall topline (40% of exports, which are 30% of W&C).

EU tariff on wires and cables is set to move from about 3.7% to zero under the announced EU trade deal, with impact likely only after around 12 months; about 40% of the company's exports go to the European Union.
Capacity from the first year of the new INR1,200 crore expansion will only start contributing from mid-FY27 onwards.
Management guided Wires & Cables volume growth of 16%-18% for FY27, ahead of industry growth.
Management guided Wires & Cables margin of 9.5% for FY27, up from the current level.
FMEG segment is now targeted to reach breakeven in FY27 after the earlier March 2026 breakeven target was missed.
Targeting 20%-25% value growth in the FMEG business in FY27, led by fans plus switchgear and appliances.
Cable contribution within the Wires & Cables segment is expected to rise by 3%-4% from the current 27%, to about 31% by year-end.

Management accepted, only as a mathematical assumption on stable commodity prices, that FY27 topline growth of about 30% is possible on 16%-18% volume growth, while declining to give rupee revenue guidance.
Company guided to FMEG segment break-even in FY27, with projected FMEG top-line value growth of 20-25%.
